site.description: Projects on writing systems: input methods, fonts, datasets and tools.
site.fonts: Specimens are drawn from the fonts named beside them, all under the SIL Open Font License.
site.title: Writing Systems
work.tangut-input: Find a Tangut character by Cangjie code, reading, parts or drawing, then read its record.
work.jurchen-input: Enter Jurchen, new in Unicode 18, by stroke code, reading, radical or drawing.
work.glyph-atlas: A dataset of character forms in pre-modern books of the Sinosphere: crops, transcriptions, code points and variants. Data under CC BY-SA 4.0, with image and text rights recorded per record.
work.ids-input: Write ideographic description sequences with a parts palette and a composed preview. Reads Han, Chữ Nôm and Tangut.
work.han-input: Find a Chinese character from whatever you know about it: a code, a reading, a part, a stroke count or a meaning.
work.han-compose: Draws a character from its ideographic description sequence as font outlines, using parts of characters the font already has.
work.han-reassemble: A quiz: put the parts of Han characters back together to find the word.
note.hangul: from the opening line of the Hunminjeongeum Eonhae
work.seokdok: A Korean input method that writes Sino-Korean words in Hanja by sound, native words in Hanja by meaning, and the rest in Hangul.
work.old-hangul-note: Type, display and convert old Hangul between Unicode, Hanyang PUA and compatibility letters.
work.koconv: A library that converts Hangul into romanizations and other scripts.
work.kureedo: A Klee One derivative with historical kana that ordinary Japanese fonts leave out, plus Ainu small kana.
work.genzui: A serif and a sans from Noto Serif and Sans JP, with hentaigana, historical kana and Unicode 18 additions.
work.honkoku-toolbox: Input helpers for transcribing classical Japanese books.
work.honkoku-client: A desktop client for Minna de Honkoku, the crowdsourced transcription platform for pre-modern Japanese documents.
work.google-ime-kana-font: A Windhawk mod that shows historical kana ligatures in Google Japanese Input's candidate window.
note.ainu: small ㇷ with a semi-voiced mark, for final p
work.ainconv: Converts Ainu words between Latin, katakana and Cyrillic. For JavaScript, Python and Rust.
work.ainukey: An Ainu input method for Windows: romaji to Ainu katakana. Early beta.
note.layout: the 訓 of 訓読, kanbun kundoku
work.writing-fails: A gallery of accidental readings caused by writing direction, layout or translation.
work.kanbun-req: Requirements for laying out annotated kanbun text, written after the W3C's Japanese layout requirements.
work.hundouk: A Typst package that renders kanbun kundoku.
note.across: Kana, kanji, Hangul, gugyeol and Tangut
